song.title: Slow Dancing In A Burning Room

guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster (Two-Tone Sunburst signature) / PRS Silver Sky
guitar.notes: Confirmed — John Mayer has had a long-documented signature relationship with Fender Stratocasters and more recently PRS Silver Sky.

tone.target: warm edge-of-breakup blues lead with long sustain
tone.profile: warm edge-of-breakup blues lead with long sustain
tone.summary: Compression -> Low Gain Boost -> US Deluxe Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab -> Guitar EQ 2 (Mid Push) -> Plate Reverb -> Digital Delay

rig.name: John Mayer - Slow Dancing In A Burning Room - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide light compression and smooth sustain.
Simulate a low-gain tube screamer/edge of breakup tone.
blocks.gap: The Blues OD is used to approximate the desired low-gain, warm grit without excessive distortion.

alternatives.reason: Slightly cleaner option if blues tone is too aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Provide a clean, articulate, and warm foundation suitable for blues lead work.
Provide a classic, balanced British voicing that complements the US Deluxe amp model.
blocks.gap: While the source suggests 2x12, the UK Vintage 4x12 offers better overall tonal depth for sustained leads.

alternatives.reason: If a smaller, more focused cabinet is preferred.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required 'slight mid push' for vocal presence and lead clarity.
Add a 'roomy plate reverb' for depth and sustain without sounding overly wet.
Add minimal delay for subtle sustain and rhythmic interest.
blocks.gap: The settings are kept low to avoid the 'aggressive delay' mentioned in the instructions.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current 4x12 IR for a more appropriate, focused 2x12 voicing.

proposals.reason: Source suggests 2x12; provides tighter focus for lead tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Tighter low end and more focused midrange clarity.
